result.markdown:
# Nationwide Latency and Core DNS Degradation Incident Report

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** core_degradation at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** high (Direct evidence of core DNS metrics deviation on CORE-DNS-01 matching the exact timing of the national latency increase, with maintenance, changes, and external events checked and ruled out.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-29 14:30 to 2026-09-29 17:30
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-29 14:30
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01

## Summary

Core DNS degradation on CORE-DNS-01 causing high resolution latency and dropped query success rates, which led to a nationwide rise in user plane latency.

Nationwide latency rose and DL volume experienced minor fluctuations while CORE-DNS-01 suffered resolution latency spikes up to 211 ms and reduced query success percentages between 2026-09-29 14:30 and 2026-09-29 17:30.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-29 13:21: A warning CPU_HIGH alarm was raised on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000645, T3]
- 2026-09-29 13:48: The CPU_HIGH warning alarm on CORE-DNS-01 cleared. [ALM-000645, T3]
- 2026-09-29 14:30: Onset of nationwide latency deviation and CORE-DNS-01 query success percentage drop and resolution ms spike. [ALR-0043, T2, T5, ANM-000443, ANM-000444, ANM-000496]
- 2026-09-29 17:30: Recovery of nationwide latency and CORE-DNS-01 performance metrics to baseline. [T2, T5]

## Evidence

- National latency_ms rose above baseline starting at 2026-09-29 14:30 and peaked at 53.4 ms. [T2, ANM-000496]
- CORE-DNS-01 query_success_pct dropped below baseline starting at 2026-09-29 14:30, reaching a worst value of 85.6%. [T5, ANM-000443]
- CORE-DNS-01 resolution_ms spiked above baseline starting at 2026-09-29 14:30, reaching a worst value of 211 ms. [T5, ANM-000444]
- No configuration changes were made on CORE-DNS-01 and its parents during the incident window. [T4]
- No maintenance windows were scheduled on CORE-DNS-01 and its parents during the incident window. [T6]
- No external events were reported across regions during the incident window. [T7]

## Hypotheses

1. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. CORE-DNS-01 experienced a severe resolution latency spike and success rate drop perfectly aligned in time with the national latency increase. [T2, T5, ALR-0043]
2. **bad_change** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. No changes were recorded on CORE-DNS-01 or its parents during the time window. [T4]
3. **planned_maintenance** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. No maintenance windows were scheduled on CORE-DNS-01 or its parents during the time window. [T6]

## Ruled out

- ALM-000645: The CPU high warning alarm on CORE-DNS-01 occurred and cleared before the incident onset at 14:30, ruling it out as the direct root cause.
- ALR-0042: Relates to an earlier single-site alert (S-SAH-008) at 10:00, which is outside the window and scope of the nationwide afternoon issue.

## Recommended actions

- Investigate the internal resource constraints on CORE-DNS-01 that caused the sudden spike in resolution time and drop in query success percentage.
- Review DNS server sizing and redundancy to mitigate potential future core bottlenecks.
